title: About keyword matching options
measures: Definitions of broad, phrase and exact match; broad match is the default match type; Google recommends Smart Bidding with broad match.
limitations: Product documentation; Google changes matching behaviour without notice.

title: About the search terms report
measures: The report lists search terms used by a significant number of people that triggered ads; low-volume terms are omitted for privacy and may be grouped as other queries.
limitations: The report does not show every query the budget paid for.

title: About negative keywords
measures: Negative keywords do not match close variants; synonyms and singular or plural forms must be added separately; account-level negative lists exist.
limitations: Product documentation; behaviour may change.

title: About advanced location options
measures: Describes the 'Presence or Interest' (default and recommended by Google) and 'Presence' targeting options and 'Presence' location exclusion.
limitations: Google's recommendation is generic and cites internal data from other verticals (travel, real estate, education), not dentistry.

title: About call assets
measures: Call assets add phone numbers to ads, can be scheduled to show only when the business can take calls, and are charged like headline clicks.
limitations: Product documentation; assets are shown only when Google's criteria are met.

title: About call reporting
measures: Call reporting uses Google forwarding numbers to record call duration, start time, caller number and connection status, and lets advertisers count calls of a specified duration as conversions.
limitations: Forwarding numbers belong to Google and can change; reporting covers calls from ads, not all practice calls.

title: Measure calls from ads
measures: Calls can be counted as conversions by minimum call duration or, where call recording is on, by Google's AI analysis of recordings (US and Canada); import-call conversions are an alternative.
limitations: Product documentation; AI-qualified call leads are a Google feature whose privacy implications for healthcare providers are not addressed on the page.

title: About primary and secondary conversion actions
measures: Primary conversion actions are used for bidding optimisation and reporting; secondary actions are observed but not used for optimisation.
limitations: Product documentation.

title: About offline conversion imports
measures: Explains importing offline outcomes using GCLID or call data; recommends enhanced conversions for leads; notes that from June 15, 2026 offline conversion and enhanced conversions for leads uploads move to the Data Manager API.
limitations: Product documentation; migration dates and recommended methods change.

title: About enhanced conversions for leads
measures: Enhanced conversions for leads uses hashed user-provided data such as email addresses to match offline conversions to ad interactions.
limitations: Product documentation; does not address whether a healthcare provider may share such data.

title: Healthcare and medicines (Google Ads policy)
measures: Restrictions on prescription drug terms in ads, landing pages and keywords; prohibition on speculative and experimental treatments; certification requirements for some categories.
limitations: Policy page; location-specific rules apply and Google updates policies without notice.

title: Personalized advertising (Google Ads policy)
measures: Health is listed as a sensitive interest category; advertisers promoting products and services in sensitive categories cannot use advertiser-curated audiences such as Customer Match, your data segments and lookalike segments.
limitations: Policy page; whether a specific dental ad is classified as health is decided by Google's review.

title: Conversions vs. key events in Google Analytics
measures: Important events are called key events in Analytics; 'conversion' refers to actions used to measure ad campaigns and optimise bidding, aligned with Google Ads.
limitations: Product documentation; terminology changed in 2024 and may change again.

title: Consent mode on websites and mobile apps
measures: Consent mode passes visitors' consent choices from a consent banner to Google tags; it does not provide a banner itself; when consent is denied, tags send pings and Google may model gaps.
limitations: Product documentation; consent mode is not in itself a HIPAA or state-law compliance measure.

title: Best practices to avoid sending Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
measures: Google policies prohibit passing PII such as email addresses and phone numbers to Analytics; PII often leaks through page URLs and titles; data redaction is available for web streams.
limitations: Product documentation; addresses Google policy, not HIPAA.

title: American Hospital Association et al. v. Becerra et al., No. 4:23-cv-01110-P, Opinion & Order (N.D. Tex., filed June 20, 2024)
publisher: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas, via GovInfo
geography: United States (federal court, Northern District of Texas)
measures: The court declared the 'Proscribed Combination' in HHS's March 18, 2024 tracking-technologies bulletin (an IP address combined with a visit to an unauthenticated public webpage about health conditions or providers) unlawful and vacated it; the rest of the bulletin was not vacated.
limitations: Court opinion; does not address authenticated pages, patient portals or other identifiers; state privacy and wiretap laws are separate. Not legal advice.

title: HHS will not appeal AHA court victory in online tracking case
measures: Reports that HHS decided not to appeal the district court decision vacating the rule in the online tracking technologies bulletin.
limitations: Published by the plaintiff trade association; the current text of the HHS bulletin could not be retrieved from this environment.

title: Portions of OCR's bulletin on online tracking technologies deemed unlawful
measures: Law-firm summary of the bulletin history (December 2022, March 2024 update) and the June 2024 ruling; states that many other aspects of the bulletin remain as subregulatory guidance.
limitations: Secondary legal commentary dated July 2024; later developments are not covered.

title: 45 CFR 160.103 — Definitions (HIPAA Administrative Simplification)
measures: Defines a covered entity to include a health care provider who transmits any health information in electronic form in connection with a covered transaction.
limitations: Regulation text retrieved through the eCFR API; whether a given practice is covered depends on its transactions. Not legal advice.

title: 16 CFR Part 318 — Health Breach Notification Rule
measures: The FTC rule applies to vendors of personal health records, PHR related entities and third-party service providers, and does not apply to HIPAA-covered entities or to entities acting as their business associates. Amended at 89 FR 47054 (May 30, 2024).
limitations: Regulation text retrieved through the eCFR API. Not legal advice.

title: 16 CFR Part 465 — Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials
measures: FTC rule text: prohibits fake or false reviews, buying reviews of a particular sentiment, undisclosed insider reviews, company-controlled review sites and certain review suppression.
limitations: Regulation text retrieved through the eCFR API (title 16 up to date as of 2026-11-05); not legal advice. State laws may add obligations.

title: Trade Regulation Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials (89 FR 68034)
measures: Final rule published August 22, 2024 with an effective date of October 21, 2024.
limitations: Publication and effective dates confirmed through the Federal Register API document record.

title: Tips to get more reviews
measures: Google prohibits offering incentives for posting, changing or removing reviews; suggests review links or QR codes; gives reply guidance, including not sharing a reviewer's private information.
limitations: Generic guidance for all businesses; its suggestion to address reviewers by name needs care for healthcare providers.

title: Prohibited & restricted content (Maps user-generated content policy)
publisher: Maps User Generated Content Policy Help
measures: Prohibits incentivised reviews, conflict-of-interest reviews, discouraging negative reviews and selectively soliciting positive reviews; merchants should not pressure on-premises reviews or request specific content, including staff quotas.
limitations: Policy page; enforcement is at Google's discretion.

title: Manage customer reviews
measures: How to reply to reviews; replies are reviewed against content policies, posted publicly as the business, and the reviewer is notified and can still change their review.
limitations: Product documentation.

title: HIPAA settlement highlights the importance of caution in responding to negative online reviews
measures: Summarises a December 14, 2022 OCR settlement in which a dental practice's replies to Yelp reviews disclosed patient names, treatment and insurance information.
limitations: Secondary legal commentary; the HHS resolution agreement page could not be retrieved from this environment.

title: California Penal Code § 632
publisher: California Public Law (reproduction of the California Penal Code)
measures: Makes it an offence to intentionally record or eavesdrop on a confidential communication, including by telephone, without the consent of all parties, with fines of up to $2,500 per violation for a first offence.
limitations: Unofficial reproduction; the official leginfo.legislature.ca.gov page could not be retrieved from this environment. Related sections (e.g. 632.7 for cellular calls) and case law affect application. Not legal advice.
